text.p: Dutch retail group Ahold NV said on Thursday its flagship Dutch supermarkets chain Albert Heijn had made a significant contribution to the overall rise in group profits in 1996.
Elsewhere in Europe Ahold businesses in Portugal and the Czech Republic achieved considerably higher operating profits.
In the United States, Ahold said, the Stop & Shop chain -- aquired last July -- contributed to a hefty rise in operating profits as did the Giant Food Stores chain.
Ahold businesses in the Asia/Pacific region were still in the start-up phase and remained loss-making, it added.
Ahold gave the following details of how sales and profits developed in 1996:

NETHERLANDS -- Overall sales rose by 4.4 pct with Albert Heijn's sales rising five pct. Albert Heijn further increased its market share as did wholesaler Schuitema, drugstore chain Etos and licquor chain Gall & Gall. Albert Heijn, Ahold Institutional Food Supply and Ahold's food production companies achieved significantly higher profits. Results at Ahold Specialty Stores (including Etos, Gall & Gall and Jamin) came under pressure from one-time write-offs. Schuitema's earnings were virtually unchanged compared with 1995.

REST OF EUROPE (Portugal, Czech Republic, Poland) -- Overall sales rose 33 pct. Excluding activities started in Poland in 1996, sales rose 29.7 pct. Local currency sales in Portugal rose 20.9 pct. Local currency sales in the Czech Republic rose 69.8 pct. Overall operating profits rose 35.1 pct. In Portugal, hypermarket chain Feira Nova showed particularly strong growth in operating profits. Operaating profits in the Czech Republic also rose significantly. Poland suffered start-up losses.

UNITED STATES -- U.S. sales rose 34.9 pct in dollars. Excluding Stop & Shop (acquired in July) rise was 8.7 percent. Giant Food Stores achieved considerable growth of sales. Tops, BI-LO and Finast also booked higher sales. Operating profits in the U.S. rose 59.5 pct in dollars, mainly because of Stop & Shop acquisition. BI-LO had lower operating results in first half of 1996 but rebounded strongly in the second half and posted a clear increase in full-year 1996 results. Giant, Edwards and Tops had higher profits in 1996. Finast produced lower results as a result of tough competition. Integration of Finast and Tops led to $25 mln in costs and provisions charged to 1996 results.
ASIA PACIFIC -- Supermarket activities were launched in 1996 in Singapore, Malaysia and China with local partners. Sales were modest and there was an overall loss due to start-up costs.
